text:
alex: Hey team — hitting javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed when calling Redwood Java SDK from behind corp proxy. Works fine from home. Any quick debug tips? Stack snippet: 
javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: Received fatal alert: certificate_unknown
	at sun.security.ssl.Alert.createSSLException(Alert.java:131) ...

priya: Sounds like TLS interception by the proxy. Can you fetch the proxy root CA and test with curl first. Example: 
```n
curl --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --cacert /tmp/corp-root.pem -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
```
If that fails, use openssl s_client to inspect the presented certs.

cam: Java doesn't use the system truststore by default (it uses the JRE cacerts). If curl + --cacert works, import into the JVM truststore: 
```n
keytool -import -trustcacerts -alias corp-proxy -file /tmp/corp-root.pem -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts -storepass changeit
```
Then restart the app.

marco: If you can't modify the JVM image, you can point at a custom truststore at runtime: 
```n
-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/path/to/corp-truststore.jks -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit
```
or build an SSLContext and pass it to the HTTP client (okhttp/httpclient).

rachel: For Redwood Private customers using mTLS, remember you also need the client key/cert in a keystore (PKCS12) and the following system props: 
```n
-Djavax.net.ssl.keyStore=/path/to/client.p12 -Djavax.net.ssl.keyStorePassword=secret
```
We usually create the p12 with openssl: 
```n
openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey client.key -in client.crt -certfile ca.pem -out client.p12
```

cam: Quick Java snippet to create SSLContext from a PKCS12 keystore + truststore (for reference): 
```n
KeyStore ks = KeyStore.getInstance("PKCS12");
try (InputStream in = new FileInputStream("client.p12")) ks.load(in, ksPass);
KeyManagerFactory kmf = KeyManagerFactory.getInstance("SunX509");
kmf.init(ks, ksPass);
KeyStore ts = KeyStore.getInstance("JKS");
try (InputStream in = new FileInputStream("corp-trust.jks")) ts.load(in, tsPass);
TrustManagerFactory tmf = TrustManagerFactory.getInstance("SunX509");
tmf.init(ts);
SSLContext ctx = SSLContext.getInstance("TLSv1.2");
ctx.init(kmf.getKeyManagers(), tmf.getTrustManagers(), null);
// pass ctx.getSocketFactory() to your HTTP client builder
```

priya: One more note — some corporate proxies terminate HTTP/2 or rewrite chunked transfers which can break streaming. If you see early stream aborts, try forcing HTTP/1.1 or setting Connection: close as a quick test. Example curl tests: 
```n
curl --http1.1 --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --cacert /tmp/corp-root.pem -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream-endpoint
```

marco: Also check if the proxy injects/strips headers (Transfer-Encoding, Content-Length). That caused our team to see partial frames. If possible, capture a tcpdump or ask proxy team for logs.

alex: OK thanks — imported corporate CA into the JRE cacerts and set -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore for the service. Handshake error is gone. Streaming still flakey; trying --http1.1 / Connection: close to see if that stabilizes. Will post logs if it persists. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: NOTE: If this is a common problem across images, please open infra ticket INF-221 to roll out the corp root CA to our base images and container JREs. (auto-generated)
